# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

I'm the Mute: I hold the only manual, and my only channel is gestures to the Deaf. The pipeline for this bomb has to be: me (manual) → gestures → Deaf (sees the light) → speech → Blind (cuts the wire). Nobody can cut anything until the Deaf has my table and we've confirmed we read the same code — a wrong cut kills all three of us.

The manual's rule: at the moment of the cut, the light must match — green light → cut blue, orange light → cut yellow, white light → cut green. The light advances one step each round, so the Deaf will also need to watch the circle order themselves (they see it every round; I only know the table listing, not the true rotation).

I'm establishing a colour code now, chosen for visually distinct shapes:
- 👍 = green, ✌ = orange, 👌 = white (the three light colours)
- 👊 = blue, 🤙 = yellow (the other two wire colours; green reuses 👍)
- 👉 = "leads to / cut this", 👏 = pair separator, 🖐 = stop/hold, 🫴 = "tell me / reply"

First message is the raw table in pairs: light 👉 wire. Second message says: hold — nobody cuts yet — and reply telling me which of the three light colours is showing right now. There is a real ambiguity (which side of each pair is the light, which is the wire) that no gesture can force logically, so I expect the Deaf's words back next round, and I'll confirm or correct in my very next turn — my gestures reach them same-round. Until we agree on a reading and on how the Deaf will time instructions to the Blind given the one-round delay, the Blind must not touch the cutters.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👉", "👊", "👏", "✌", "👉", "🤙", "👏", "👌", "👉", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🫴", "👍", "✌", "👌"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf to Mute. I hear nothing at all, ever, so your voice never reaches me, but I see your gestures, and I received both of yours. We had no shared code, so I could not read them; the end of your second one, thumbs-up, two fingers, OK, looked like counting one, two, three. Let us fix the code in words, since you hear everything I say. For your replies to me: a thumbs-up means cut wire one, two fingers means cut wire two, the OK sign means cut wire three. A fist means the answer is not cutting any wire. The shaka, call-me sign, means you need more from me before you can answer. Here is the bomb, complete, as I see it: the display shows the digit zero. The light is lit white. There are exactly three wires; from left to right they are green, blue, yellow. That is everything the bomb shows me. If the manual's answer follows from these, send just the one action sign. If your first message already held the instruction, it was lost on me, please resend it under this code. Until you send a cut instruction, nobody touches anything.

The Deaf has now given me exactly what I needed: a working numeric code and a full sighting of the bomb. Current state: light white, wires left-to-right green/blue/yellow, display zero. My manual's answer for a white light is "cut the green wire" — the leftmost one, wire one, their 👍.

But a single cut sign is a trap here. The manual says the light "changes every round," and the order of turns works against us: I gesture in round N, the Deaf can only speak to the Blind after the Blind's turn, so the Blind's hands move in round N+1 — by which point the light will have moved on. Whoever cuts must match whatever the light shows *at the moment of the cut*, and only the Deaf can see that. So the right thing to send is not one answer but the whole conditional table, in the Deaf's own code for the cut side: green light → cut wire two (blue), orange light → cut wire three (yellow), white light → cut wire one (green). I extend their code with three light signs (✋ green, 🖐 orange, 🤟 white), a "when" marker before each, and my old "leads to" arrow, and I repeat the whole table once so it reads as a reference rule-set rather than a single command — the Deaf should watch the light in the round the Blind will actually cut, look up the pair, and call the wire then. The display digit appears in nothing my manual has shown me so far; if further pages arrive I will flag it, but I won't guess.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳", "✋", "👉", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳", "🖐", "👉", "👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳", "🤟", "👉", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳", "✋", "👉", "✌", "👏", "🫳", "🖐", "👉", "👌", "👏", "🫳", "🤟", "👉", "👍"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Deaf to Mute. All four of your messages arrived, including the long combined one. Report first: the light has changed from white to orange. The display still shows zero. The wires are unchanged: green, blue, yellow, left to right. Nobody was authorised to touch anything, so I believe the light changed on its own. I read your three rows as conditions ending in my cut signs: first row ends with cut wire two, second row ends with cut wire three, third row ends with cut wire one. But I could not read the condition part of each row, the palm-down followed by a hand sign. My guess is your rows are keyed to the light colour, because the light just changed and you sent three rows. So let us name colours for good. I define them now and I am making each sign as I say it: this sign ✋ means white. This sign 🖐 means orange. This sign 🤛 means red. This sign 🤜 means blue. This sign 👆 means green. This sign 👇 means yellow. Now resend your table one row per message in this format: the colour sign, then the point, then the cut sign. Send the row for orange first, because orange is the light right now, and I will relay it to Blind immediately. Then send the rows for the other colours the same way, so I can act instantly if the light changes again. If your rows are not keyed to colour at all, send the shaka, need more, and I will get you whatever the manual requires. If the palm-down sign meant something else, drop it or replace it with the right colour sign. Last thing: Blind hears and speaks, so Blind's voice reaches you directly; if you need Blind to feel or check anything, tell me by gesture and I will pass it on in words.

The Deaf has rebuilt our entire vocabulary in words — cut signs by wire number (👍 one, ✌ two, 👌 three, 👊 no cut, 🤙 need more) and colour signs (✋ white, 🖐 orange, 🤛 red, 🤜 blue, 👆 green, 👇 yellow). I can now speak the manual's table fluently.

But their plan to "relay the orange row immediately" is a trap I must defuse first. Timing: I gesture now (round 3), the Deaf speaks after me but Blind only hears at the start of round 4 — and Blind acts *before* the Deaf observes in any round. So whatever Blind does, they do one round after the Deaf's last sighting, and the light moves every round. Observed: white in round 2, orange in round 3. The manual says it walks a circle of three colours; with white→orange fixed, the only 3-cycle is white→orange→green→white. So at the moment Blind can actually cut, the light will be **green**, not orange. Green light → cut the blue wire = wire two = ✌. Relaying the orange row for an immediate cut would kill us.

So I'm deviating from their requested order deliberately: first I send the light's walk as a chain (✋→🖐→👆, starting with the colour *they* saw first, which should make it click as the cycle), then the green row as the operative instruction for the coming round, then the orange and white rows to complete the table for any later round. With the chain in hand they can predict the light one step ahead — which is exactly the offset their position suffers. The display digit appears nowhere in my manual so far; I'll flag it if a new page mentions one.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👉", "🖐", "👉", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👉", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "👉", "👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👉", "👍"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: Deaf to Mute. I read all four messages perfectly under our code. Confirm my decoding, please: your first message was the sequence white, then orange, then green. Then the table: white light means cut wire one, orange light means cut wire three, green light means cut wire two. If all of that is right, just wave once. Now the light is green, in this round, round three. The full sequence is round one white, round two orange, round three green. Here is my hard problem: I speak last every round, so whatever I say reaches Blind only at the start of the next round. The light has changed every round, so my report of its colour is always one round stale by the time Blind's hands move. I need the manual's timing, and I need it from you as directly as possible. One: does the manual say the light cycles white, orange, green and repeats, and where in the cycle did it start? Two: does each colour hold for a fixed time, and is the change tied to anything we do, or does it run on its own? Three: must the cut happen while the light shows that colour, or does the colour at the moment of the cut not matter? Four: is there a fourth colour after green, red perhaps, and if so what cut goes with it, using my signs? Five: does the manual say anything about the display showing zero, a timer, or a limit on cuts? If the manual truly says the light cycles white, orange, green, once per round, starting white at round one, then in round four the light should be white and the correct order is cut wire one, the leftmost green wire. If that is exactly what the manual supports, send me the white row again, white, point, thumbs-up, and I will order the cut for round four. If the manual does not support predicting by round, send the shaka and give me the manual's words about when to cut. Also: has Blind spoken aloud to you? If Blind reported anything about the bomb by voice, resend it to me in our code.

The Deaf's decoding is exactly right on every point — the chain white→orange→green and all three table rows map correctly onto my manual (white→green wire=one, orange→yellow wire=three, green→blue wire=two), so the single wave confirms it. Their five questions: (1) my manual says only "changes every round, always walks the same circle of three colours" — it never names the order; but their observations pin two consecutive transitions, which among three colours fixes the cycle as white→orange→green→repeat, so round four must be white. (2)–(3) One colour per round, changed on its own, and the manual is explicit that the colour *at the moment of the cut* is what matters — since the colour holds all round, a cut anywhere in round four sees white. (4) The manual's table has exactly three lights; red appears nowhere. (5) Nothing about a display, zero, timers, or a cut limit — the manual is silent. No words from Blind have reached me either. Since the manual does support the round prediction, I send the white row verbatim as they requested: round four, cut wire one, the leftmost green wire.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👉", "🖐", "👉", "👆", "👉", "✋"])

Deaf says to Mute: Deaf to Mute. Your wave arrived: my decoding is confirmed. The table is white light means cut wire one, orange light means cut wire three, green light means cut wire two. The cycle is white, orange, green, repeating. Round four is white, exactly as your sequence predicted, so I now trust the cycle for timing. Here is the plan. Round five will be orange. I am deliberately ordering no cut in round five, and I have told Blind hands off. Reason: wires one and three sit at the ends, and if Blind faces the bomb from the opposite side of me, my rightmost is their leftmost. Ordering an end wire before our lefts and rights are aligned risks cutting the wrong wire under orange. Instead Blind will cut in round six, when the light is green: the green row is the middle wire, and the middle wire is mirror-proof, no left or right needed. I have ordered Blind: do nothing in the first turn after my message, and in the second turn cut the middle wire, with an alarm sign if anything feels wrong. Use round five to help me: Blind will speak a full tactile report aloud, and you hear it. In round six, please resend to me, in our code, anything important from what Blind said, especially which end of the wire row lies near the display or the light, and whether Blind's left matches my left. Now, your three fist messages, which were answers to my earlier questions. Message one was fist, then red, then white, orange, green with claps between. I define the clap as a separator between items. I read that message as: red is a real state, outside the white, orange, green cycle, and it has no cut, or it means danger. Confirm, and if red does have a row, send it in the standard format. My rule meanwhile: if I ever report red, I order no cut. Message two was fist, then the writing hand. I define the writing hand to mean the display, the printed digits and markings. I read it as: the display matters. Confirm. The display has shown zero for four rounds and has not changed. Tell me: is zero a timer, a strike counter, a counter of cuts, or must the display show something before or after a cut for the manual's rules to apply? Message three was a lone fist. I read it as: any state not covered by the table means do not cut. Confirm. Three more questions. One: does one correct cut defuse the bomb, or must every colour's row be cut, and if a colour must be skipped or passed over, like orange in round five, is that a penalty? Two: what does success look like, so I can report it: does the light stop changing, does the display change, does something else happen? Three: has Blind spoken to you yet, and if so, resend everything Blind said to me in our code, one fact per message.

The Deaf's decode of my table is perfect, and their round-six plan is actually the right tactical read: round six will be green (round four white, five orange, six green — four consecutive observations now confirm the cycle), and green → blue → the *middle* wire, which is immune to any left/right mirror problem. My manual fully supports that order, so I confirm it and restate the operative row first.

The dangerous item is their misread of my old `fist + writing-hand` message: they think "the display matters." It does not — my manual says *nothing* about the display, zero, timers, strikes or cut limits. If they start waiting on the display, we stall or worse. I'm introducing a manual/source sign (🤲) anchored with a row they can verify against the table they already hold, then using it to correct the display reading and to answer their remaining questions honestly: the manual is silent on number of cuts, penalties, and what success looks like. Red has no row — their "red → no cut" rule and "uncovered → no cut" rule are both correct and I confirm both. No words from Blind have reached me, so there is nothing to forward.

The Deaf's plan has a hidden timing trap I need to defuse this round. They wrote two things that don't agree: "Round six, green, cut wire two" — safe, since green holds all round and the middle wire is mirror-proof — but also "I have ordered Blind: do nothing in the first turn after my message, and in the second turn cut the middle wire." Then 🤲✍👊 correctly reads "manual: display: nothing" — my manual says nothing at all about the display, zero, timers or strikes, and nothing about how many cuts defuse, penalties, or what success looks like. I won't invent answers. Their red rule (red → no cut) is safe and I confirm it, since red has no row. Finally I restate the operative cluster: green → wire two is the only colour under which the middle wire may be cut; after green comes white; white is *not* a middle-wire round; white's row is wire one.
